behavior: An empty `id` counts as no `id`, as a prop or as an attribute of a part. The part then has the id that it has with no `id`, and each part that names it names that id. Base UI keeps an empty `id` in most parts. The element then has `id=""`, which HTML does not allow, and no ID reference can name it. A dialog, a popover, a menu, a group, a fieldset, a meter, a progress bar, a tab panel or a toast then has no name. A field, a dialog, a popover or a toast loses its description, and a label names no control. Two sliders, selects, comboboxes or date fields with `id=""` give the same derived ids, and the second slider takes the name of the first. Base UI's `Collapsible.Panel`, `Accordion.Trigger` and `Checkbox.Root` already treat an empty `id` as no `id`. An `id` of white space only also counts as no `id`. HTML allows no white space in an id, and white space separates the ids of an ID reference, so no reference can name such an id. Base UI keeps such an id in each part, also in those three parts.
